notes: Summary: Evaluating Redwood for company-wide document search + customer support assistant. Strong fit functionally but P&L doesn't work at current unit economics; procurement paused all external AI commits starting Nov.

Discovery (2024-09-05): CTO Mark Alvarez: heavy emphasis on precision and audit trail. Typical queries ~1.2k tokens (avg) with many long-context searches (5k+ tokens occasionally). Latency target: 100-200ms tail for support flows; throughput bursty during peak support hours.
Architecture ask: VPC + KMS integration, 90-day audit logs, role-based access + SSO. Interested in dedicated pools to guarantee latency; want canary + fallback to cheaper model if quality acceptable.

Cost sensitivity: Finance model shows break-even requires <$0.0009/token for generation-heavy flows or large commit discounts. They modeled GPU costs for fine-grained reranks and found hosted per-token cost plus embedding units resulted in A/B failure vs competitor bundled offerings.

Work done: SE ran cost projection (Ravi) with caching and quantization scenarios. Optimistic config (aggressive prefix caching + 4-bit quant) reduces token spend by ~30% in simulation, still above their internal target unless commit > $120k/yr.

Security: No blockers on SOC2/KMS; legal wants explicit data residency SLA for EU customers — potential future Ask.
Open items: Exec-level cost model that maps token spend to customer LTV; legal sample contract with data residency clause; proposal for 6-month pilot with strict usage cap and rollback triggers.

Next steps suggested by AE: 1) Draft a lightweight pilot contract (6mo, $40k commitment, built-in throttles). 2) Provide IO-level cost model tied to LTV scenarios. 3) Re-engage in Jan after budget review. 4) Keep SE on standby for architecture Qs.

Winback signals to monitor: signs of easing of procurement freeze; competitor pilot hitting quality issues; inbound from legal requiring on-prem proof-of-concept.
